chapter_title: Measuring AI Capability: The METR Task-Horizon Studies
learning_objective: The learner will classify eight example systems into the narrowest of six categories (Not AI, AI without machine learning, Machine learning, Generative AI, Large language model, AI agent), correctly placing at least seven of eight on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: infographic **sim-id:** ai-terms-classifier
**Library:** html
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** classify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will classify eight example systems into the narrowest of six categories (Not AI, AI without machine learning, Machine learning, Generative AI, Large language model, AI agent), correctly placing at least seven of eight on the first attempt. **Template:** https://github.com/dmccreary/ai-strategy-for-education/tree/main/docs/sims/ai-concept-hierarchy
**Prerequisites:** artificial intelligence, machine learning, generative AI, large language model, AI agent (all defined in the section "A Ladder of Terms" above). **Evidence of Mastery:** The learner places each of 8 examples in one of six category bins and submits it. A placement is correct when it matches the "Correct category" column in Content. Mastery is 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Opening the category definitions is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Any software that feels smart is AI. (2) All AI is machine learning. (3) A chatbot and an agent are the same thing. **Instructional Rationale:** Classifying requires recognizing which defining feature an example has, such as learning from data, creating content, or taking multi-step actions. Choosing the narrowest category forces the learner to use the nesting, not just the topic word. **Content:** Six categories, shown as nested regions from outside in (Not AI sits outside all the others), each with its definition shown on selection: | Category | Definition shown | |---|---| | Not AI | Software that follows a fixed rule and does nothing that requires intelligence | | AI without machine learning | A system that performs an intelligent task using rules or search written by programmers | | Machine learning | A system that learns patterns from examples in order to label or predict | | Generative AI | A machine-learning system that creates new content, such as images or audio | | Large language model | A generative AI system trained on text to produce language | | AI agent | A system built on a language model that takes multi-step actions with tools toward a goal | Eight examples: | # | Example shown to the learner | Correct category | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | A thermostat that switches the heat on whenever the room is below 68°F. | Not AI | It follows one fixed rule and does not do anything that requires intelligence. | | 2 | A 1990s chess program that scores positions using rules its programmers wrote. | AI without machine learning | It plays chess, an intelligent task, but nothing was learned from data. | | 3 | An email filter trained on millions of messages labeled spam or not spam. | Machine learning | It learned from labeled examples and only labels; it creates nothing new. | | 4 | A model that estimates which students may fail a course using past grades and attendance. | Machine learning | It learned a pattern from past data to predict; it does not create content. | | 5 | A tool that draws a new picture from a sentence describing it. | Generative AI | It creates new content, but images are not language. | | 6 | A tool that turns a typed sentence into new spoken audio in a chosen voice. | Generative AI | It creates new audio, and it is not a language model. | | 7 | A chatbot that answers a teacher's question in several paragraphs and cannot take any other action. | Large language model | It generates language and stops after answering. | | 8 | A system told "build a quiz website" that writes code, runs it, reads the error messages, and fixes them over many steps. | AI agent | It plans and takes many actions with tools to reach a goal. | **Provenance:** Definitions follow the chapter section "A Ladder of Terms: From AI to AI Agents." The examples are illustrative, written for this chapter. **Rules:** Each example has exactly one correct category: the narrowest category whose definition it meets. An example is scored on its first submitted placement only. The score counts first-attempt correct placements out of 8. Mastery is a score >= 7. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one example at a time and the six categories. 2. The learner places the example and submits. The sim marks it correct or incorrect and shows the feedback text. 3. If incorrect, the learner may place it again; the second attempt does not change the score. After the second attempt, the correct category and reason are shown. 4. After all 8 examples, the sim shows the score and lists misplaced examples with their correct categories. 5. The learner should notice that examples 3 and 4 use machine learning for different purposes and land in the same category, and that examples 7 and 8 both use a language model and differ only in whether they take actions. **Feedback:** 8 examples, shuffled once per session, two attempts each. Correct: "Correct: [category]. [Why text]." Incorrect: "Not quite. [Why text for the correct answer, without naming the category]." After the second attempt the correct category is revealed and the example counts as missed. A running score "First-try correct: n of 8" is shown. Final message for a score >= 7: "You can place AI systems on the ladder." For a score < 7: "Review the definitions and try again; the examples will be reshuffled." **Starting State:** The nested regions are shown with example 1 of the shuffled order, the score "First-try correct: 0 of 8," and the prompt "Which is the narrowest category that fits this system?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter names six categories in the order Not AI, AI without machine learning, Machine learning, Generative AI, Large language model, AI agent. The chapter states that every LLM is generative AI and every generative system is machine learning. The mastery bar is 7 of 8.
